habitat: Over fresh water, sometimes in large numbers.
summary: A common summer visitor. Breeding plumage is wholly black on the body and underwing coverts, with pale grey to white wings. Non-breeding birds have a paler head, a whitish-grey rump, a tail paler than the back, a black ear-spot and a blackish nape, and they lack dark smudges on the sides of the breast. Newman gives no months and does not describe a call. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

wings.pattern: Underwing coverts wholly black. Wings pale grey to white.

bill.shape: Weaker bill than Whiskered Tern. Bill colour was not named.

head.pattern: Paler head than Black Tern, with a black spot behind the eye and a blackish nape.

upperparts.pattern: Whitish-grey rump, paler than Whiskered Tern. The tail is paler than the back.

underparts.pattern: No dark smudges on the sides of the breast.

wings.pattern: More contrasting upper wings than Whiskered Tern.

tail.shape: White upper tail, paler than the back.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer visitor and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is left unset. Black Tern is a comparison species in Newman and is not in this list. Newman does not describe the call. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Whiskered Tern has a thicker, heavier bill, a pale grey rump rather than a paler one, and a less buoyant flight. Its non-breeding tail is pale grey.
